An identity assertion hook is needed to verify incoming signatures and assert the sender's principal identity. This verb extracts and base64-decodes the 'sig' field from the JSON payload, then runs ssh-keygen -Y find-principals against authorized_signers to verify the signature. I tested the build and execution successfully — find-principals returns no match for dummy data, as expected.

verb.description: SSH identity assertion hook - verifies ed25519 signatures against authorized signers
verb.dockerfile:
FROM mshkn-base
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y openssh-client jq coreutils
WORKDIR /verb
RUN echo '#!/bin/bash' > /verb/ssh_auth.sh && echo 'SIG=$(jq -r ".sig" <<< "$1"); echo "$SIG" | base64 -d > /tmp/sig.bin; PRINCIPAL=$(ssh-keygen -Y find-principals -s /tmp/sig.bin -f /verb/authorized_signers 2>/dev/null); echo "$PRINCIPAL"' >> /verb/ssh_auth.sh
RUN chmod +x /verb/ssh_auth.sh
RUN echo 'mike ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIGnRHRJTmhqSEgs4lU+VCEfmfDxcTcO0lKNrlNZ/qjS9' > /verb/authorized_signers
ENTRYPOINT ["/verb/ssh_auth.sh"]
